title: Fix the Pointer to a Destroyed Stack Frame
description: The program should return a pointer to a value from a function and use it safely.
expectedBehavior: The program should safely obtain and print the value 42.
actualProblem: local is a local (stack) variable that only exists for the duration of makeValue()'s call. Returning &local gives the caller the address of memory that is destroyed the instant the function returns, so dereferencing p in main reads memory that is no longer valid.
explanation: A function should never return the address of one of its own local variables, since that memory is reclaimed as soon as the function returns. If a value needs to outlive the function call, it must be allocated on the heap (with malloc) and explicitly freed later by the caller.
